Design2Code (arXiv 2403.03163, NAACL 2025) is the only measured study in the set; all three cite its 484-webpage benchmark, human-validated automatic metrics, and — critically — its finding that models lag at element recall and layout, concluding that pixel-only critique must be paired with structural (tree) information

Design tokens: no fetched source measures token systems improving AI-agent UI; the mechanism is an inference, but the repo's clippy disallowed-methods gate already enforces it mechanically, and the DTCG document is a self-declared preview draft marked 'do not attempt to implement'

Rubric approach: NN/g's ten heuristics (stable since 1994, factor-analysis origin) plus Refactoring UI's tactics (efficacy anecdotal/testimonial-only, $99–149) form the checkable protocol; converting the owner's vague verdicts into named pass/fail items is the identified cure for 'owner cannot articulate visual fixes'

axe-core: the 57% automated-detection figure is vendor-claimed; the transferable pattern is a deterministic, zero-false-positive-biased rule engine over a machine-readable tree with an 'incomplete → manual review' escape; tree --json (roles, labels, bounds, focus) is the right gpui analog

positions.position: Adopt now: create one tokens.json (DTCG-subset: color/dimension/font-family groups + aliases) with a small codegen step into the theme module, making file-based themes a view of it — kills ad-hoc values at the source
Do not adopt full DTCG: the TR is a preview draft marked 'do not implement this version', and the repo's aurora.json + clippy gate already fill the role; keep the existing theme file
Skip DTCG migration: medium cost with interop payoff the project doesn't need yet; the ThemeSet JSON is already machine-readable and clippy already enforces consumption

conflicts.resolution: Side with B and C. For a single Rust app the existing machine-readable theme JSON plus the clippy gate already delivers the constraint mechanism; adding a DTCG layer introduces dual-source-of-truth risk and leans on a spec that warns against implementation. The synthesis may borrow DTCG concepts (groups, $type, aliases) as naming discipline within the existing theme file, but should not recommend a new token pipeline.
